title: An Analysis of Social Biases Present in BERT Variants Across Multiple Languages
benchmark_measurement: Stereotypical associations between religious groups and negative concepts, such as violence or being 'backward', measured via sentence pseudo-likelihood scores in template-based probes.
findings: Religious biases were found to be highly language-dependent and reflective of cultural contexts. English and Greek models showed significant associations between Islam and violence, and between Hinduism and backwardness. The Persian model exhibited a strong bias against Judaism and, in some contexts, Islam. These biases are hypothesized to correlate with user-generated content in the models' training corpora and reflect specific cultural or historical narratives.
